previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A young woman with a history of tracheobronchomalacia, laryngeal stenosis, bronchopulmonary dysplasia, and tracheostomy dependence was admitted for evaluation of worsening dysphagia and odynophagia. She reported a three-day history of sore throat and difficulty swallowing, with coughing after liquids. Initial workup showed normal labs and a clear chest X-ray. Speech and swallow evaluation revealed improved swallowing with tracheostomy occlusion, and an EGD showed no mechanical obstruction. Her symptoms were attributed to pharyngeal residue, and she was successfully managed with behavioral strategies. She tolerated a regular diet with technique modification, remained stable, and was discharged home with follow-up instructions.

Brief Hospital Course:
===================
SUMMARY:
===================
___ with a history notable for tracheobronchomalacia and 
bronchopulmonary dysplasia secondary to premature birth at 
___, s/p 4 airway reconstructions and tracheostomy since 
infancy, history of chronic bronchitis and recurrent tracheitis, 
as well as chronic supraglottic stenosis and laryngeal stenosis 
who presented to the ED with recurrent dysphagia. During this 
hospitalization, she was able to resume eating a regular diet 
with good pain control. Barium swallow showed the patient to 
have moderate esophageal dysmotility.

===================
ACUTE ISSUES:
===================
#Dysphagia
#Moderate esophageal dysmotility
#Throat pain, odynophagia
On admission, the patient reports dysphagia above baseline with 
a globus sensation, as well as throat pain (without swallowing) 
and odynophagia, both above baseline. She was admitted in ___ with a similar presentation, at which time evaluation was 
overall unremarkable and she was recommended a particular 
protocol (3 swallows with 1 solid food bolus, 2 swallows with 1 
liquid food bolus, and occluding trach with each food bolus to 
improve swallowing pressure and bolus flow). The patient noted 
relatively weak adherence to this regimen at home. During this 
admission, IP saw the patient and felt her dysphagia and 
odynophagia to not be related to the trach. ENT saw the patient, 
performed bedside endoscopy, and noted only bilateral turbinate 
hypertrophy and right septal spur as well as supraglottic 
hyperfunction but no significant explanation for her symptoms. 
Video swallow showed mild oropharyngeal dysphagia without 
aspiration, as well as frequent cough after swallowing, though 
to be due to hypersensitivity. They felt her to be safe to 
resume s regular diet. Barium swallow showed moderate esophageal 
dysmotility, which previous barium swallow had not shown. In 
terms of her diet, she was initially NPO and then advanced, and 
by discharge was tolerating a normal diet and pills/capsules 
without significant issues. Pain control was provided with 
standing Tylenol, NSAIDs, and lozenges with good relief.

#Hyperglycemia
Fasting blood sugar of 160s-170s on morning labs. Thus, A1c 
checked and found A1c 7.9 this admission.

===================
ACUTE ISSUES:
===================
#Tracheobronchomalacia
Tracheostomy since birth, followed by IP as an outpatient. Had 
routine tracheostomy change on ___ and tracheobronchial 
wash. Per IP this admission, trach appears to be without issue.

#Asthma
The patient was continued on home home inhalers/nebs.

#Depression/anxiety
The patient was continue on home fluoxetine.

___: Mother/HCP

===================
[]SWALLOWING TECHNIQUES: Please continue to monitor the patient

food bolus, 2 swallows with 1 liquid food bolus, and occluding

Discharge Instructions:
Dear Ms. ___,

It was our pleasure taking care of you at the ___ 
___!

WHY WERE YOU ADMITTED TO THE HOSPITAL?
- You were having difficulty swallowing at home and had throat 
pain, especially with swallowing.

WHAT HAPPENED IN THE HOSPITAL?
- You were seen by the Interventional Pulmonologists, who 
determined that your tracheostomy was in the right place and 
your swallowing issues were not related to it.
- You were seen by the Otolaryngologists who performed endoscopy 
at the bedside. This did not find an explanation for your 
swallowing issues.
- You were seen by the Speech Language Pathologists, who helped 
you work on strategies to improve your swallowing. They felt 
that you were safe to resume a normal diet.
- You underwent a video swallow, which did not show any 
aspiration of food contents into your airways.
- You underwent a barium swallow, which showed that you had 
moderate esophageal dysmotility, meaning your esophagus does not 
move as it normally should.
- You were provided pain control and given IV fluids until you 
were able to resume a regular diet.

WHAT SHOULD YOU DO ONCE YOU LEAVE THE HOSPITAL?
- Please take all your medications as prescribed and attend all 
your doctor's appointments.
- Please continue to work on the swallowing techniques you 
developed with the help of the Speech therapists, which includes 
3 swallows with 1 solid food bolus, 2 swallows with 1 liquid 
food bolus, and occluding trach with each food bolus to improve 
swallowing pressure and bolus flow.
- Please see a gastroenterologist about the esophageal 
dysmotility. You can arrange this appointment through your 
primary doctor.
- Please be conscious of your diet. Your blood sugars were high 
in the hospital, meaning that you may have diabetes. You should 
see your primary doctor about this.

We wish you all the best!
Your ___ Healthcare Team
